items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: We had a very fine bassist named Clarence Jones, and Chuck Thompson, an excellent drummer, was around here some of the time... We all would play on Sundays out there.

ctx.x: it, see, in the first part of the week there. And oh, we had a lot of... All the fine players used to come through there and play.

In the meantime, Hampton Hawes, the pianist, he was coming out of high school just about the time that Sonny was coming out of school. So we all would play on Sundays out there. And Wardell Gray had moved out here, and we would play out there... We had some fantastic sessions out there on Sunday. We had a very fine bassist named Clarence Jones, and Chuck Thompson, an excellent drummer, was around here some of the time, and Roy Porter was around here... Oh, they had a lot of great players...
That group really kind of stayed together. Because when I started going to dances just a few years later, in 1949, you were there every Sunday, no matter where the session was...
